## Loading Libraries

```{python}
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.svm import SVR
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
import polars as pl
import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd
```


## Introduction

This document demonstrates how to do continuous predictions using functions from the sklearn library. We will also do a simple marketing mix modeling analysis.


## Load and Prepare Data

```{python}
# Load the dataset
data_url = "Gaming and Mental Health.csv"
data = pl.read_csv(data_url)

# Drop unused columns
data = data.drop(["gender", "age"])

# Drop rows where the target variable is null
data = data.drop_nulls(subset=["work_productivity_score"])

print(f"Rows after removing nulls in target: {len(data)}")
data.head()
```


## Specify Feature and Target Columns

```{python}
target = "work_productivity_score"
numeric_features = ["sleep_hours", "daily_gaming_hours", "grades_gpa"]

# Drop rows where any feature column is null
data = data.drop_nulls(subset=numeric_features)
print(f"Rows after removing nulls in features: {len(data)}")

# Preprocessor — only numeric features, no empty categorical list
preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        ('num', StandardScaler(), numeric_features)
    ]
)

# Split into train and test sets
train, test = train_test_split(data.to_pandas(), test_size=0.5, random_state=11109)

print(f"Train size: {len(train)}, Test size: {len(test)}")
```


## ML Pipelines

```{python}
lr_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', preprocessor),
    ('model', LinearRegression())
])

rf_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', preprocessor),
    ('model', RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=50, random_state=11109))
])

svm_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', preprocessor),
    ('model', SVR())
])
```


## Train and Predict

```{python}
# Fit models and generate predictions
lr_pipeline.fit(train[numeric_features], train[target])
train["lr_prediction"] = lr_pipeline.predict(train[numeric_features])
test["lr_prediction"] = lr_pipeline.predict(test[numeric_features])

rf_pipeline.fit(train[numeric_features], train[target])
train["rf_prediction"] = rf_pipeline.predict(train[numeric_features])
test["rf_prediction"] = rf_pipeline.predict(test[numeric_features])

svm_pipeline.fit(train[numeric_features], train[target])
train["svm_prediction"] = svm_pipeline.predict(train[numeric_features])
test["svm_prediction"] = svm_pipeline.predict(test[numeric_features])
```


## Compute Error and RMSE

```{python}
# Convert test to Polars for error computation
test_pl = pl.DataFrame(test).with_columns([
    (pl.col("lr_prediction")  - pl.col(target)).alias("lr_error"),
    (pl.col("rf_prediction")  - pl.col(target)).alias("rf_error"),
    (pl.col("svm_prediction") - pl.col(target)).alias("svm_error"),
])

# Compute RMSE for each model
rmse = test_pl.select([
    pl.col("lr_error").pow(2).mean().sqrt().alias("lr_rmse"),
    pl.col("rf_error").pow(2).mean().sqrt().alias("rf_rmse"),
    pl.col("svm_error").pow(2).mean().sqrt().alias("svm_rmse"),
])
print("RMSE for each method:")
print(rmse)
```


## Visualize Predictions vs Actual Values

```{python}
# Convert back to pandas for Plotly (consistent behavior across versions)
test_pd = test_pl.to_pandas()

def predict_vs_actual_plot(df, prediction_col, mytitle):
    fig = px.scatter(
        df,
        x=target,                  # FIX: was 'purchase_amount' (wrong column)
        y=prediction_col,
        title=mytitle,
        labels={target: "Actual Work Productivity Score", prediction_col: "Predicted Value"},
        trendline="ols"
    )
    fig.show()

predict_vs_actual_plot(test_pd, "lr_prediction",  "Linear Regression: Predicted vs Actual")
predict_vs_actual_plot(test_pd, "rf_prediction",  "Random Forest: Predicted vs Actual")
predict_vs_actual_plot(test_pd, "svm_prediction", "SVM: Predicted vs Actual")
```


# Marketing Mix Modeling Example

```{python}
marketing_url = "https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=15UaT_hXyPQ5y_jVzkIAiEik6f-IrV51l"
marketing = pd.read_csv(marketing_url)

feature_mmm = ["youtube", "facebook", "newspaper"]
target_mmm  = "sales"

marketing_lr_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ("lr", LinearRegression())
])

marketing_lr_pipeline.fit(marketing[feature_mmm], marketing[target_mmm])

coefficients = marketing_lr_pipeline.named_steps["lr"].coef_

coef_df = pl.DataFrame({
    "Feature":     feature_mmm,
    "Coefficient": coefficients.tolist()
})
print("Marketing Mix Model Coefficients:")
print(coef_df)
```
